tool_registration.seam_as_found: The port pattern described in CLAUDE.md and in inspect_stage.py's docstring is accurate and was followed: pure function under the cognitive layer, schema registered alongside, adapter branch swapped in call_tool(). Three drifts from that description are recorded below rather than silently adapted to.

seam_drift.claim_in_docs: 'the Dispatcher is the single entry point through which tool calls reach Houdini' (dispatcher.py:3-5)
seam_drift.as_found: There is no single Dispatcher. mcp_server.py builds FOUR independent Dispatcher singletons - _inspector_dispatcher (mcp_server.py:596), _scout_dispatcher (:721), _ported_dispatcher (:829) and now _blocks_dispatcher - each with is_testing=True and its own transport closure over the asyncio loop. M5 follows the established four-singleton practice, not the one-Dispatcher prose.

seam_drift.claim_in_docs: Dispatcher's production path marshals to Houdini's main thread via main_thread_executor (dispatcher.py:295-314)
seam_drift.as_found: Every dispatcher in mcp_server.py is constructed with is_testing=True and no main_thread_executor; the production _execute_via_main_thread branch is unwired and raises NotImplementedError. Main-thread safety on this path is provided downstream by the WS execute_python handler inside Houdini, not by the Dispatcher. M5 inherits exactly that posture and claims nothing more.

seam_drift.claim_in_docs: Inspector precedent inlines the whole Houdini-side implementation into a template string (tool_inspect_stage.py:119-257)
seam_drift.as_found: M5 deliberately does NOT. The injected script is three flat lines calling synapse.blocks.runtime, because the F-1..F-5 harness imports and runs that same module directly under hython. Inlining would mean the harness proved something other than what the tool executes. Recorded as an intentional divergence from the precedent, with the reason.

findings.title: The committed fixture baseline is cwd-dependent - it embeds $HIP
findings.detail: karmarendersettings authors $HIP/render/<hipname>.<node>.####.exr into the composed stage, and $HIP resolves to the process working directory for an unsaved scene. probes._build_fixture_once run from this worktree yields 6552415dc1452483380f3a896db3a3a06d1d51cc34b9afe25dafac617e456b2d; run from C:/Users/User/SYNAPSE it yields the committed 8bb05761... byte-exact. The fixture's baseline block records sha256, build, canonicalizer and verified_run but NOT the $HIP or cwd, and harness/autoresearch/runs/fixture_verify_20260805_182646/ records no environment either. The baseline is therefore machine-local and undocumented as such.
findings.mitigation: The invariant harness PINS $HIP via hou.putenv rather than depending on launch directory, defaults it to the repository's MAIN working tree (resolved from the .git file/dir without shelling out), refuses to run if the pin did not take, and records hip_before_pin / hip_after_pin / hip_pin_effective in every evidence file.

findings.title: createNode('domelight') produces type name 'domelight::3.0' - naive type comparison never converges
findings.detail: The fixture declares type 'domelight'. The created node's type().name() is 'domelight::3.0'. Comparing the fixture literal against the raw type name reported a permanent mismatch, so every apply planned delete+recreate of dome_light, apply_fixture never converged (applied=false, status=incomplete, residual_ops=2), and F-3 could never have been green. nodeTypeCategory().nodeType('domelight') does NOT resolve the version - it returns the unversioned entry - so the stable identity is NodeType.nameComponents()[2] == 'domelight', which observe() now records as type_base. A fixture that declares a versioned literal still matches exactly.
findings.found_by: the F-1..F-5 harness, via apply_fixture's own post-mutation self-verification returning applied=false rather than a false success

findings.title: createNode and createNetworkBox and setName all auto-rename SILENTLY on a name clash
findings.detail: stage.createNode('null','syn_probe_n1') on a taken name returns a node called 'syn_probe_n3' and raises nothing. createNetworkBox('SYN_PROBE_BOX') on a taken name returns 'SYN_PROBE_BOX1'. box.setName('SYN_PROBE_A') onto a taken name silently yields 'SYN_PROBE_A1'. This is why D2's collision gate MUST run before creation: detecting the clash afterwards is impossible without having already mutated the scene. Both create paths additionally re-assert the resulting name and destroy + raise on drift, as a second line of defence.
findings.pinned_by: runtime._create_node and the box branch of apply_fixture; F-5

findings.title: NetworkBox.destroy() defaults to KEEPING its members
findings.detail: Signature is destroy(self, destroy_contents=False). Probed empirically: after box.destroy() both member nodes were still alive in /stage. remove_fixture therefore enumerates members, destroys each explicitly, then destroys the box - which is also the shape D3 wants (enumerate, never pattern-match).
findings.pinned_by: F-2 (the stage between remove and re-apply is asserted empty of both nodes AND boxes)

findings.title: A String parm's authored value is unexpandedString(), not eval() - and eval() would have hidden a real bug
findings.detail: The camera node's DEFAULT primpath is '/cameras/$OS', which EVALUATES to '/cameras/camera' - byte-identical to what the fixture declares. Comparing on eval() would have reported the node already correct and never authored the literal, leaving the fixture's value unset while every check read green. Comparing on unexpandedString() is correct and idempotent. Caveat recorded: unexpandedString() raises hou.OperationFailed('Cannot get unexpanded string for parms with keyframes'), so _read_parm falls back to eval() for keyframed parms - a keyframed parm cannot be authored as a literal anyway.
findings.pinned_by: F-1 (the composed hash would differ if the literals were unauthored) + F-3

findings.title: A network box is USD-neutral - D1 and the F-1 oracle are compatible
findings.detail: The fixture's baseline was cut by a builder that creates NO box; the reconciler creates one. Building the fixture with and without the box in the same session yields an identical composed hash. Had this been false, D1 and the oracle would have been in direct conflict and F-1 could never have been green. Checked before writing reconciler code, not assumed from the fixture's own note.
findings.corroborates: fixtures/solaris.basic.json:8 'boxes have zero effect on composed USD'

findings.title: The LOP display flag is one exclusive network-wide slot
findings.detail: setDisplayFlag(True) on node B clears it on node A. Two consequences. (1) A planner 'clear the display flag on the wrong node' list could never fire usefully, so it was removed rather than shipped as a check that cannot fail - Law 1. (2) A fixture that declares a display node cannot be honoured without taking the slot from whoever holds it, possibly an artist node outside the box. See R-M5-2.

findings.title: Comparing a destroyed hou.Node raises hou.ObjectWasDeleted
findings.detail: list.remove() on a destroyed node raises from Node.__eq__. The reconciler therefore captures member NAMES before any destroy pass and re-resolves each by name inside the loop; it never holds node handles across a destroy.
findings.pinned_by: runtime.remove_fixture (member_names captured before the loop) and the delete branch of apply_fixture

findings.title: The canonicalizer seam adds a RuntimeWarning to the autoresearch harness under plain Python
findings.detail: probes.py now imports from the synapse package, which triggers synapse/__init__.py's vendored-SDK ABI check. On stock Python 3.14 (runner.py --validate-only) that emits a RuntimeWarning to stderr, landing in run.err.log, which Get-AutoResearchState tails when there is no heartbeat yet. Cosmetic and truthful, but new noise in a harness that previously had none. Under hython (3.13) it does not fire. Recorded rather than suppressed - the warning is telling the truth about the environment.

for_ruling.question: The solaris.basic baseline embeds $HIP and is therefore machine-local. Re-baseline against a pinned synthetic $HIP, record the $HIP in the fixture, extend the canonicalizer to strip $HIP-derived paths, or leave it and keep pinning in the harness?
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I - a value judgement about what a number should be. Any of the four is defensible and each costs something different: re-baselining invalidates the committed sha256; recording $HIP documents the limit without removing it; a c3 canonicalizer rule is a re-baseline event for every future fixture; leaving it keeps the oracle honest but only on this machine.
for_ruling.shipped_meanwhile: The harness pins $HIP, defaults to the repo's main working tree, refuses to run if the pin did not take, and records the pinned value in every evidence file. No fixture was modified.

for_ruling.question: Honouring a fixture's declared display node necessarily moves the network's ONE exclusive display flag, possibly off an artist's node. Keep honouring it (shipped), honour it only when the box is first created, or never take the flag from a node outside the box?
for_ruling.why_escalated: This is the one place where 'make /stage match the definition' and 'artist nodes untouched, always' genuinely cannot both hold - they contend for the same single slot. It also changed what F-4 asserts, so it is not a hypothetical.
for_ruling.shipped_meanwhile: Honour the fixture, and report the transfer by name: result['display_taken_from'] and ['display_taken_from_outside_box']. The invariant was SPLIT rather than softened - F-4 now pins that every AUTHORED property of the artist node is unchanged, and a NEW F-4b pins that the display transfer is reported instead of silent. Options 2 and 3 were rejected because both make the fixture's declared display permanently unsatisfiable when an outsider holds the flag, which would leave residual_ops=1 forever and break idempotence.

for_ruling.question: A node the artist dragged INTO our box, which the fixture does not declare, is currently DELETED on the next apply. Delete it (shipped), or eject it from the box and leave it in /stage?
for_ruling.why_escalated: D1 says membership in the box IS ownership and D3 permits deleting box members, so deleting is the direct reading and is consistent with remove_fixture, which deletes members by ruling. But ejecting cannot destroy artist work under any circumstance, and the asymmetry matters: a wrong delete is recoverable only by Ctrl+Z, a wrong eject by dragging.
for_ruling.shipped_meanwhile: Delete, chosen for consistency with remove_fixture's ruled behaviour, with every deletion reported in result['deleted'] and per_node carrying the reason 'not declared by the fixture'. No invariant distinguishes the two, so switching to eject is a small, contained change.

for_ruling.question: The committed h22 symbol table is stamped 22.0.397 while the installed and fixture-targeted build is 22.0.368. Regenerate for 368, accept 397 as the H22 authority, or stamp a build-range?
for_ruling.why_escalated: Not M5's to decide and not load-bearing for M5, but it is a standing correctness question for synapse_scout's phantom gate on this host.
for_ruling.shipped_meanwhile: Nothing. M5 verified every API claim by direct runtime probe on 22.0.368 rather than by table lookup.
